scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: One squeeze of a fire extinguisher, and the flames are gone. But how does it actually kill a fire?

scenes.name: triangle
scenes.text: Fire needs three things: heat, fuel and oxygen. Take away any one, and it goes out.

scenes.name: water
scenes.text: Water extinguishers cool the fire, removing heat. They're good for wood and paper, but dangerous on oil and electrical fires.

scenes.name: co2
scenes.text: Carbon dioxide extinguishers push away oxygen and cool a bit. They suit electrical fires and leave no residue.

scenes.name: powder
scenes.text: Dry powder ones coat the fuel, and interrupt the chemical reaction of burning. They work on many fire types.

scenes.name: inside
scenes.text: Inside, a pressurised gas pushes the agent out when you squeeze the handle.

scenes.name: pass
scenes.text: Remember PASS. Pull the pin, aim at the base, squeeze, and sweep side to side. And leave if it's too big.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Heat, fuel, oxygen. Break the triangle. Follow for more on how things really work.
